From purchase brief to first restore

  1. Choose where it runs

    I size the workload and give you a purchase brief. You place the order and control billing.

    Choose infrastructure

  2. Build and connect the stack

    I configure your CRM, file storage, VPN, and single sign-on. We agree on who needs access, what to back up, and how to test recovery.

    Browse applications

  3. Train the people who will run it

    Your administrator practices a restore with their own credentials. I hand over the configuration, runbooks, and an AI troubleshooting assistant connected to approved sources in your environment.

    See what you receive

What stays in your hands

Infrastructure and accounts
You own equipment you buy. For rented infrastructure, your business holds the provider account, billing, and administrator access.
Code and data
You keep the project code, deployment repository, data exports, and backup access. Upstream software keeps its own license.
One project payment
The agreed open-source stack has $0 per-seat licensing and no recurring fee to me. Budget for your team’s time and any infrastructure or storage you buy from providers.

Questions before you start

What does the one-time payment cover?

We agree on the deployment, integrations, migration, recovery checks, and training before I quote one implementation fee. You buy infrastructure and any third-party services in your name.

Will self-hosting cost less?

It depends on your current bills, the hardware or provider you choose, and who maintains the stack. Run the comparison with your own costs over one, three, or five years.

Who runs the system after handoff?

Your designated administrator handles updates, alerts, and recovery. We practice these tasks during handoff.

Can you build a website or store in my accounts?

Yes. I can deploy a website or store in your accounts, document its integrations, and train your team to edit and operate it.

Tell me what you want to build or replace

Include the tools you use today and who will run the system after handoff.
